item: The columnar cache's encryption key is stretched like the corpus's (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 x 256,000 over the passphrase and a per-store salt in a sidecar), is bound to the ATTACH as a parameter and never written into its text, and a guard fails on any fast hash of a passphrase-like name under src/ and scripts/

summary: The persisted DuckDB cache was keyed by one SHA-256 of the passphrase (CodeQL py/weak-sensitive-data-hashing; disclosed, not fixed, in the 2026-09-17 OPEN_QUEUE entry), a cheaper offline attack on the one passphrase that also opens the corpus behind PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 x 256,000. _derive_key is now hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac(sha512, passphrase, salt, 256_000) with the count SQLCipher's own (a test reads it back from a live connection; the derivation is pinned against OpenSSL's answers) and a random 16-byte salt per store in the sidecar analytics.duckdb.kdf (atomic, owner-only, under a lock, destroyed by the crypto-erase and the uninstall together with the engine's log analytics.duckdb.wal); a store without a valid v2 sidecar is removed and rebuilt, never opened. The key is a bound parameter of the ATTACH and the path's quotes are doubled, because measured with DuckDB 1.4.4 and 1.5.5 a path with an apostrophe made a parse error quote the first 16 to 24 characters of the key, which no exact-match scrub finds; the gate attaches the same way with a random key and takes no passphrase, and connect and refresh_persisted_read_model log their failures through log_failure with the passphrase and the key (the passphrase guard holds the module). tests/test_passphrase_hashing_guard.py fails on any fast hash (hashlib but pbkdf2_hmac and scrypt, hmac, a hash object's update) of a name that says passphrase, password, pw or secret, or of anything made from one, across 754 files, with an empty allow-list; what a stretching call makes is not followed (a keyed HMAC of a stretched key passes) and a secret/pw/pwd name that is not the passphrase is flagged too. No shipped build opens the persisted store yet; a derivation costs about 0.21 s. A real-engine test with DuckDB's software backend (run by the columnar CI lane, which did not name the file) and a stronger CI-only httpfs round trip cover the statement. Seventy-three mutations are each caught. What stays outside is in OPEN_QUEUE.md.
